data.long_meaning: Mihira is derived from the Sanskrit word 'mihira' which means 'goddess of the sun'. In Hindu mythology, Mihira is the goddess of light, wisdom, and creativity. The name Mihira carries the meaning “Goddess of the Sun” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mihira usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of the sun and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Mihira is an ancient Sanskrit name, deeply rooted in Hindu culture and mythology. In India, it is believed that the name carries the blessings of the sun god, Surya, who is the embodiment of power, energy, and light. Hence, a child named Mihira is considered to be blessed with divine light and energy from the sun god, bringing happiness, prosperity, and good fortune to the family.
data.spiritual_significance: Mihira signifies the presence of light and wisdom in one's life. It is believed that a person named Mihira is endowed with the qualities of purity, brilliance, and enlightenment. The name is a constant reminder of the importance of seeking knowledge, truth, and inner light in one's spiritual journey, just like the sun that illuminates the world around us. Therefore, Mihira is a name that inspires seeking knowledge, inner peace, and spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Mihira is a Sanskrit name meaning "the one who brings light". It is associated with the sun god, Surya, and symbolizes the inner light of consciousness and self-illumination.

The name is also believed to be derived from the Sanskrit word 'mih' meaning 'shining', and is therefore a fitting name for a baby girl who is expected to bring light and radiance into the world.
